title: Drupal says core flaw CVE-2026-132165 was exploited on live sites; fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13
summary: Drupal rates SA-CORE-2026-017, CVE-2026-132165, highly critical: under specific conditions install.php can be used to reinstall a site, leading to takeover or code execution. In an update to the advisory, Drupal says its Security Team received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. A second advisory, CVE-2026-132166, is a gadget chain that is not directly exploitable.
plain: Drupal fixed a serious flaw that can let an attacker take over a website by re-running its installer, and says it has a report of the flaw being exploited on live sites.
exec: Drupal has a report that this highly critical flaw was exploited on live sites; Drupal sites on older versions need its fix.
action: Drupal advises updating core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13; if you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes. Older branches are end of life, per Drupal.

key_findings: SA-CORE-2026-017 (Highly critical, CVE-2026-132165): installer reinstall leading to takeover or RCE; advisory update reports exploitation on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC.
SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166) is a gadget chain needing a separate unsafe-unserialize flaw.
recommendations: Upgrade; secure the installer if you cannot.

validation.note: Read both Drupal security advisories (primary); NCSC-NL also lists the release. SA-CORE-2026-017 re-read on 22 November: it now carries an update reporting exploitation on live sites and the score 'Highly critical 20 / 25 ... E:Exploit'.

review.note: Compared CVE, critical rating, PoC (E:Proof), fixed versions, EOL branches and Anthropic OSS Scanner credit against SA-CORE-2026-017 and -018

evidence.quote: Update: the Security Team has received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC.
